selected.title: My Sister Asked Why I Banned Her From My Wedding
selected.hook: My sister called crying and asked why I'd banned her from my wedding.
selected.voiceover:
My sister called crying and asked why I'd banned her from my wedding. The problem was, I hadn't.

Our wedding was six weeks away, and she'd been my maid of honor since the day we got engaged. She said my fiance had called her that morning and told her she was no longer invited unless she apologized to his mother.

I thought she was joking.

Two weeks earlier, his mom had criticized my sister's dress at a family dinner. My sister told her, politely, to stop commenting on her body. It was awkward, but I thought it was over.

Apparently my fiance didn't.

He told my sister that his mom deserved respect, that I was too stressed to handle more drama, and that he'd made the decision for me.

Then he asked her not to contact me until she was ready to apologize.

When I confronted him, he said he was protecting our wedding from conflict.

But then my sister sent me screenshots.

He'd also messaged two of my cousins, warning them that anyone who upset his mother could lose their invitation.

He had basically created wedding rules in my name without telling me.

I told him every invitation stays exactly as it is, and if anyone needs to reconsider attending, it's the person issuing secret ultimatums.

Now he says I'm choosing my family over him before we're even married.

Would you postpone the wedding after this, or is that going too far?
selected.youtube_description:
Six weeks before her wedding, her maid-of-honor sister called in tears asking why she'd been banned from the ceremony. The bride had never banned her at all. A family disagreement quickly exposes secret wedding ultimatums, messages sent in the bride's name, and a much bigger fight over loyalty and control. Would you still walk down the aisle?
